decision_reason: Included because a protocol-guided LLM policy agent proposes regional interventions from weekly epidemic surveillance series and checks them through counterfactual rollouts of a learned action-conditioned epidemic world model before selection, a scored decision task over time-indexed data analogous to Neuro-Agentic Control.

decision_reason: Included because the LLM agent retrieves cut-off-bounded events and updates reflective retrieval memory and causal knowledge from realized forecast errors on time-series targets.

evaluation_summary: Six domains (weather and electricity 7-day, stock next-day direction, memory/SSD prices 6/9 months, Polymarket probabilities) with chronological learning/evaluation windows; MAE/MSE, accuracy and Brier score against seven deep forecasters, six LLM-based forecasters, TimesFM 3.0 and Chronos-2, plus no-event and event-RAG ablations over four backbone LLMs.

title_checked: GIFT-Eval-CTX: A Benchmark For Contextual Forecasting Model Evaluation
decision_reason: Included because the benchmark's structured temporal context is constructed by tool-using LLM agents with deterministic validators (BatteryLake precedent) and its evaluation scores a tool-using agentic forecaster alongside TSFMs and LLMs.
agent_claim_evidence: Title/abstract explicitly describes an agentic annotation pipeline and benchmarks tool-using agentic systems.
claim_summary: GIFT-Eval-CTX builds 10,000 hard GIFT-Eval test windows annotated with structured Macro and Micro future effects through validator-gated discovery agents and a blind-first critic, and measures how well forecasters convert that verified context into numerical trajectories.
task_family_original: Forecasting and prediction; time series annotation
evaluation_summary: 10,000 instances from 20 GIFT-Eval datasets (78 dataset-term groups, horizons 30-900 steps); aggregate relative MASE for four TSFMs, GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 4.8 under paired history-only and history-plus-effects conditions, and a GPT-5.6 Sol MoiraiAgent with Moirai-2 forecasting and code-execution tools, with Macro/Micro, effect-family and inside/outside-region breakdowns.

modules.name: Validator-gated structured temporal effect annotation
modules.scope_reason: Agents propose trend, seasonality and interval-bounded excursion, mean-shift or seasonal-change effects that deterministic validators recompute from the raw series; the schema and checks describe any series segment and would survive a change of task family, although the residual overview tool here uses TSFM forecasts.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "the pipeline first runs independent"
evidence.quote: the pipeline first runs independent Macro and Micro Discovery Agents, each combining LLM reasoning with deterministic code validation. The LLMs identify informative regions, determine effects’ mechanism and boundaries, and submit proposals. Deterministic validation then checks the proposed type and type-specific criteria. If a proposal fails validation, the tool returns the numerical evidence so that the Agent can revise its proposal.

evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "Free-form descriptions confound the information"
evidence.quote: Free-form descriptions confound the information conveyed by a context with its wording, domain vocabulary, and level of detail. We instead represent future context through structured effects, a domain-agnostic key-value schema designed to be portable across models. Structured effects decompose the future into a single Macro description and a set of Micro effects.

function_view.rationale: The pipeline produces temporal context annotations and validates each proposed effect's type, boundaries and intensity against the raw series before acceptance.

modules.name: Blind-first joint critic review

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "Blind-first Joint Critic Agent. After"
evidence.quote: Blind-first Joint Critic Agent. After both discovery branches finish, a Joint Critic Agent reviews their outputs. The Critic first inspects the raw history and future while all outputs of the discovery agents remain hidden. Only after forming an independent interpretation can it view the proposed Macro and Micro effects, their explanations, and the corresponding numerical evidence.

agent_claim_evidence: Title/abstract explicitly describes an agent or benchmark for agents.
claim_summary: ACE-Trader runs a Commit-Challenge-Revise loop between an LLM Trader and Red-Team, picks each role's memory with selectors trained online on memory-on versus memory-off net-return differences, and settles critiques and revisions against realized outcomes to build linked role-specific memories.
evaluation_summary: Daily trading of 33 U.S. equities with 2021-2023 FNSPID data for baseline training and warm-up and a 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30 test on FMP data with 5 bp costs; cumulative and annualized return, Sharpe, drawdown, volatility, hit rate and turnover against 22 active baselines in six categories (ML, RL, general and finance LLMs, single- and multi-agent trading systems) and two passive references, plus selector/co-evolution ablations and alpha/gamma sensitivity.
corrections: Cumulative return (+12.44%) is slightly below NASDAQ buy-and-hold (+12.82%); the advantage over the passive index lies in Sharpe, drawdown and volatility, not return.

modules.name: Net-return-trained context-dependent memory selectors
modules.scope_reason: Selector inputs combine market and portfolio features, and labels come from net-return differences between memory-assisted and memory-free trading pipelines, so the mechanism is bound to the trading objective.

evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "Each selector combines a frozen"
evidence.quote: Each selector combines a frozen semantic encoder with an ensemble of trainable feedforward networks to score candidate memories using the current decision context, including market conditions, together with memory content and recorded outcomes.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "Once the outcomes are observed"
evidence.quote: Once the outcomes are observed, the net-return difference provides a shared binary label, with near-tied outcomes excluded. Each selector is trained on the saved representations of its selected memories using recency-weighted binary cross-entropy. The trading LLMs and semantic encoder remain frozen.

function_view.rationale: Recency-weighted selection of past experience conditioned on the current market state realises context memory, bound to a net-return label.

modules.name: Outcome-settled Trader and Red-Team memory co-evolution
modules.scope_reason: Critiques carry observable conditions and evaluation horizons that are settled against realized prices, and revision benefit is the net-return difference between portfolio plans, so the memory content is defined by trading outcomes.

evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "We also check the risk"
evidence.quote: We also check the risk warnings in ct against the conditions and evaluation times specified before execution. A warning is a hit if the observed outcomes satisfy its stated condition under the specified evaluation rule. It is a false alarm if its evaluation horizon has ended and sufficient observations show that the condition was not satisfied.

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "The Red-Team issues a challenge"
evidence.quote: The Red-Team issues a challenge only when current evidence contradicts a specific assumption in the Trader’s proposal. Each challenge includes suggested portfolio adjustments and a risk warning specifying an observable condition and when it should be evaluated.

function_view.rationale: Warnings are settled only after their stated horizon and outcome-dependent experience enters memory only once observed, realising horizon-aware validation and context memory for the trading task.

title_checked: Training-Free Continual Learning for Multimodal Forecasting via Prompt Evolution
decision_reason: Included as a boundary work because an LLM reflection loop evolves a forecasting policy from realized-outcome feedback on time-series windows, although the system is not described as an agent.
agent_claim_evidence: No Agent terminology for the system; included as an outcome-driven LLM reflection loop with feedback over time-series forecasting windows.
claim_summary: The work evolves a plain-text guidance block for a frozen LLM forecaster through GEPA-style reflection on forecast-versus-realized traces, parent gating and Pareto selection, under knowledge-cutoff contamination control, and optionally compiles the guidance into code that calls a TSFM.
evaluation_summary: Refreshed TimesX (weekly search indices, daily currencies, daily commodities; 96-step history, 12-step target, dated news); GM MASE on a 249-window final tier (origins Sep-2025 to Mar-2026) against TimesFM-2.5, TabPFN-TS-3, Chronos-2, unguided Llama-3.3-70B and Claude Opus 4.6, and SeasonalNaive, with transfer, compiled-code, horizon and news-removal ablations and one executed re-adaptation cycle.
corrections: All findings rest on one benchmark family with three domains and one window geometry; the multi-period continual deployment is proposed, with only one cycle executed.
LLM arms receive calendar, holiday and sibling-series context that the numeric-only TSFM baselines do not, and the authors leave this information gap uncontrolled.
notes: Identity and selected method/evaluation passages checked against local PDF text; not an independent reproduction of reported results.

modules.name: Outcome-gated forecasting guidance evolution
modules.scope_reason: The reflector rewrites forecasting guidance from forecast-versus-realized traces and per-window MASE, and children are gated and Pareto-selected on forecast error.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "2. Reflect. The reflector reads"
evidence.quote: 2. Reflect. The reflector reads the minibatch’s full execution traces (raw histories, complete news context, forecast vs. realized paths, per-window MASE, rationales) and rewrites g freely; only ex-ante usability, generality, and the word cap bind. 3. Gate. The child must beat its parent on the same minibatch or is discarded.

function_view.rationale: The evolved guidance is a persistent text context distilled from resolved forecasting windows and injected into the frozen forecaster's prompt.

modules.name: Cutoff-postdating tiers with untouched monitor
modules.scope_reason: Windows are admitted by their origin relative to each model's knowledge cutoff and consumed at separate rates; this availability-time control does not depend on the forecast output and applies to other LLM tasks on time-indexed data.

evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "Cross-model experiments with Claude Opus"
evidence.quote: Cross-model experiments with Claude Opus 4.6 (Aug-2025 cutoff) use only origins after September 2025. Optimization consumes data at three rates: a selection tier consulted every iteration (optimistic by construction); an untouched monitor never used for decisions, whose gap to selection measures overfitting; and final tiers set postdating every model’s cutoff touched exactly once for evaluation.

function_view.rationale: Origins postdating model cutoffs and an untouched monitor separate optimization, overfitting measurement and one-time final evaluation.

modules.name: Guidance-to-code compilation with TSFM tool

evidence.locator: PDF p.6; passage beginning "(1) A coding LLM (Claude"

title_checked: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
decision_reason: Included because FairAMO is a controlled evaluation protocol for agentic orchestration of time series foundation models, including an LLM-mediated orchestrator, scored on forecasting under frozen candidates and commit-before-reveal evidence.
agent_claim_evidence: Title/abstract explicitly describes evaluation of agentic model orchestration; the taxonomy names LLM-mediated orchestration (MoiraiAgent, TimeCopilot) as one class.
claim_summary: FairAMO evaluates TSFM orchestrators on a frozen forecast bank where each must commit a selection or weights from a fixed backtest budget before test labels are revealed, separating orchestration ability from candidate-pool strength and complementarity.
evaluation_summary: GIFT-Eval official test split with a five-TSFM main pool; 11 deployable orchestrators (reference rules, five external methods, re-trained MoiraiAgent and a patch router) scored by official MASE against the best single TSFM and a window-level oracle, with pool-size, evidence-budget and composition sweeps.
corrections: Only MoiraiAgent-Retrained is LLM-mediated and TimeCopilot is evaluated through its median ensemble, so the results bound orchestration generally; the paper itself states the contribution of LLM-mediated orchestration remains unclear.
Conclusions are limited to GIFT-Eval with one committed decision per config and backtest-only evidence; they do not test agents that use context beyond backtests.
notes: Identity and selected method/evaluation passages checked against local PDF text; not an independent reproduction of reported results.

modules.name: Frozen forecast bank with commit-before-reveal orchestration
modules.scope_reason: The cached state is candidate quantile forecasts per rolling origin and the committed action is a model selection or combination weights scored by forecast error, so it is tied to the forecasting output contract.

evidence.locator: PDF p.2; passage beginning "we introduce FairAMO, a controlled"
evidence.quote: we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol built on a Frozen Forecast Bank. Within each comparison, all orchestrators operate on the same candidate forecasts and receive the same explicitly specified historical evidence. Each orchestrator must commit to either a model selection or a set of combination weights before the test labels are revealed, and all resulting forecasts are evaluated using the official GIFT-Eval protocol.

evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "Before any test label is"
evidence.quote: Before any test label is revealed, the orchestrator receives the permitted evidence: the N most recent training backtests, plus the validation backtests if available. Using only this evidence, it produces an orchestration strategy, either a model selection or a set of combination weights, which is then committed and frozen for the test period. No rerun, reweighting, or inspection of test scores is permitted after commitment.

function_view.rationale: Committing decisions from only the most recent permitted backtests before test labels are revealed realises leakage-free temporal validation for forecast orchestration.

modules.name: Pool headroom and realization decomposition
modules.scope_reason: Headroom, gain and realization are defined from forecast losses of the best single TSFM, the window-level oracle and the orchestrator, so the metric is bound to forecast selection and combination.

evidence.locator: PDF p.7; passage beginning "• Headroom H(P ) ="
evidence.quote: • Headroom H(P ) = Lbest (P ) − Loracle (P ) is the accuracy that the differences between pool members put on the table. It is a property of the pool alone and does not depend on the orchestrator. • Gain G = Lbest (P ) − Lmethod (P ) is what a method actually recovers relative to the baseline. It is negative for a method that ends up worse than the best single TSFM, which several of the methods we evaluate do.

function_view.rationale: The recorded contribution implements a task output, objective, supervision procedure or task evaluator rather than one of the four shared-function rows.

adjudication_note: Kept as a boundary benchmark: the protocol targets agentic orchestration of forecasters, but only one evaluated orchestrator is LLM-mediated.

title_checked: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
decision_reason: Included because it is a benchmark and public leaderboard that scores LLM agents' iterative quantitative research loops over date-scoped A-share market series by the sealed out-of-sample trading performance of their committed strategies.
agent_claim_evidence: Title/abstract explicitly describes an agent or benchmark for agents.
claim_summary: Quant-Arena has LLMs write feature and stock-scoring code over raw daily and Level-2 A-share data, revise it with bounded research-period feedback, and freeze one strategy that a cash-account evaluator assesses on a sealed out-of-sample year.
evaluation_summary: A 3,042-stock A-share universe with daily and Level-2 data; research on 2022-2023 with at most five candidate evaluations and sealed assessment on 2024; nine frontier models at every supported reasoning effort (38 iterative and 38 one-shot configurations) are scored by composite S, annualized and excess return over the gross equal-weight market, RankIC, long-only Sharpe and maximum drawdown, with Kepler-1 and the market as references.

The sealed-period score uses an unpublished combination rule, and the leading Kepler-1 entry is a proprietary strategy from the authors' organisation whose method is not disclosed.

modules.name: Date-scoped market data interface
modules.scope_reason: Access is gated by decision date, instrument and field with identical rules in research and assessment, a point-in-time availability constraint that would serve a forecasting or other market-series task without redesign.

evidence.locator: PDF p.3; passage beginning "Missing observations and delisted stocks"

At each decision date, the strategy can access authorized historical observations, including permitted warmup history. The same input definitions and access rules apply during research and assessment.

modules.name: Bounded research loop with sealed-year assessment
modules.scope_reason: Feedback, the frozen deliverable and the sealed evaluator are defined around a stock-scoring program converted to a top-75 equal-weight cash-account portfolio, so the protocol is bound to the trading-strategy output contract.

evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "Models may evaluate candidate strategies"

evidence.locator: PDF p.4; passage beginning "At the end of research,"

title_checked: Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core

evidence.locator: PDF p.5; passage beginning "The labels the Evening Analyst"

title_checked: Agri-SCHOLAR: Simulation-Grounded In-Season Rolling Advisories for Agricultural Crops Using LLM-Bounded Optimization
decision_reason: Included because LLM agents issue weekly, simulator-scored irrigation and fertilizer decisions from as-of daily weather series (observed, short-range forecast and analog-year tail), a scored decision task over time-indexed data analogous to the retained trading agents and to Neuro-Agentic Control.
agent_claim_evidence: Title/abstract explicitly describes an agent or benchmark for agents.
claim_summary: Agri-SCHOLAR issues weekly in-season irrigation and fertilizer advisories in which LLM agents set agronomically feasible action bounds and an optimizer searches within them, scoring each candidate with APSIM on a weather trajectory restricted to information available at the decision date.
evaluation_summary: Eleven kharif maize seasons (2015-2025) in one irrigated and one rainfed South Asian region with ERA5 daily weather; weekly advisories are replayed in APSIM under realized weather and compared with the regional package of practices on yield, net profit, production cost and sustainability penalty, with loose-bound and no-bound ablations of the bounding agent (Gemma-4-E4B-it agents).
corrections: All outcomes are APSIM simulations (the simulator is not calibrated against field trials) and the seven-day forecast is a synthetic perturbation of observed weather, so the gains do not establish field yields or performance with operational forecasts.

In the irrigated-region ablation, loose expert-range bounds give higher mean yield and profit than the LLM bounds; the demonstrated benefit of the LLM bounding agent is a lower sustainability penalty and agronomically practical doses, not higher profit.
notes: Identity and selected method/evaluation passages checked against local PDF text; not an independent reproduction of reported results.

evidence.quote: The key component of Agri-SCHOLAR is a novel LLM-bound optimization mechanism that assigns complementary roles to language agents and numerical optimization. evidence.quote: The VFA translates each candidate action into APSIM tool calls and runs the simulation on the constructed weather file for the current cycle. It also returns them to the ABA, so that bounds can be tightened or relaxed if they repeatedly yield infeasible or dominated candidates.

title_checked: From extreme weather to agricultural consequences with agentic AI
decision_reason: Included because a tool-using LLM assistant answers hazard and crop-loss questions for past and forecast dates by invoking daily county weather-hazard indices and a calibrated loss model computed from weather series, a decision-support use of time-indexed weather data in the same family as the retained AI-Meteorologist and SIREN weather agents.

claim_summary: WxCrop is an LLM assistant that routes plain-language questions to tools computing causally selected daily county hazard indices from weather records and forecasts and a payout-calibrated crop-loss model, assembling every reported number from tool receipts.
evaluation_summary: 67 Florida counties, 2004-2024, with USDA RMA cause-of-loss insurance records: hazard indices scored by AUC against recorded cyclone, freeze and severe-drought days or seasons (0.98, 0.99, 0.76); leave-one-year-out loss model reproduces summed storm-month losses within 2%, ranks county citrus production declines (rank correlation 0.63) and UF/IFAS county pairs (66% correct), with payout-probability Brier 0.177 versus 0.224 for historical frequency; the assistant is shown through Hurricane Ian, freeze and dry-heat case studies.
corrections: The LLM assistant (GPT-6 Sol) is not evaluated quantitatively; every reported check concerns the non-LLM hazard indices and loss model, and the assistant appears only in case-study screenshots.

Loss checks are strongest for hurricanes; freeze and dry-heat percentages are checked only against scarce records (extreme freezes a factor of two to five below reports), and outputs are county-level percentages on the insured-unit scale, not field-verified losses.
